points.quote: the use of any type of generative artificial intelligence tools (such as text generating, image generating, computer software generating, and translators) is not permitted in your assignment unless your module leader has explicitly specified that their use is permitted
points.gist: Generative AI tools of any type are not permitted in an assignment unless the module leader has explicitly said their use is permitted.

points.quote: you should never just copy and paste content produced by generative AI and present it as your own work, to do so would likely be considered Academic Misconduct.
points.anchor: Can I use generative AI in my work?
points.gist: Never copy and paste generative AI content and present it as your own work; this would likely be treated as Academic Misconduct.

points.quote: If your work is thought to contain content that you did not create yourself, it can lead to a lengthy investigation and very serious consequences.
points.anchor: Academic misconduct and referencing generative AI
points.gist: Work thought to contain content you did not create yourself can lead to a lengthy investigation and very serious consequences.

points.quote: Consider what you are being assessed on and whether generative AI is appropriate.
points.anchor: Can I use generative AI in my work?
points.gist: Consider what you are being assessed on and whether generative AI is appropriate.

points.quote: if you’re a Games Design student being assessed on your ability to draw a character concept, is presenting work produced solely by DALL-E or Midjourney appropriate?
points.anchor: Can I use generative AI in my work?
points.gist: Example question: is presenting work produced solely by DALL-E or Midjourney appropriate for a Games Design student assessed on drawing a character concept?

points.quote: Do not share any personal, confidential, or sensitive information. Any data entered into generative AI can be fed into the data sets that the generative AI relies upon
points.gist: Do not share personal, confidential or sensitive information, because data entered into generative AI can be fed into its data sets.

points.quote: You should not enter any personal, sensitive, or confidential data. This goes for your own personal data (like asking a generative AI to write a CV for you) but also any research data that you might collect via primary research.
points.anchor: Legal, ethical, and data protection considerations
points.gist: Do not enter personal, sensitive or confidential data, including your own personal data such as for a CV, or primary research data.

points.quote: Do not rely on generative AI as a source in itself, such as referencing a definition or piece of information on a topic. Generative AI is not a credible academic source.
points.gist: Do not rely on generative AI as a source in itself; it is not a credible academic source.

points.quote: Always cross-reference the information, including any references, presented with more valid academic sources.
points.gist: Always cross-reference information, including references, against more valid academic sources.

points.quote: Referencing can be used to acknowledge the use of AI generated content, but this is generally limited to situations where you are including AI generated content as stand-alone examples that are clearly set apart from the main body of your work.
points.anchor: Academic misconduct and referencing generative AI
points.gist: Referencing to acknowledge AI content is generally limited to stand-alone examples clearly set apart from the main body of your work.

points.quote: AI generated text should be referenced as a personal communication, because the responses generated are unique to you (they are non-reproducible).
points.gist: In Harvard, AI generated text should be referenced as a personal communication because responses are unique to you and non-reproducible.

points.quote: You should check with your lecturer or module-leader whether you should include the transcript of your interaction as an appendix to your work. For maximum transparency, we recommend this as a good approach.
points.gist: Check with your lecturer or module leader whether to include the interaction transcript as an appendix; this is recommended for maximum transparency.

points.quote: They can make up information and/or reproduce false information from the web, including citations and references.
points.anchor: What are the limitations of generative AI?
points.gist: Generative AI can make up information or reproduce false information from the web, including citations and references.

points.quote: Web-based technologies like generative AI have a significant environmental impact.
points.anchor: Legal, ethical, and data protection considerations
points.gist: Web-based technologies like generative AI have a significant environmental impact.

points.quote: If you don’t understand how to use generative AI or need some advice on which tools to use, then the Library’s Digital Skills Advisors are able to help.
points.gist: The Library's Digital Skills Advisors can help if you don't understand how to use generative AI or need advice on tools.
